slides.title: What Are Methods
slides.content: Methods are reusable blocks of code that perform a specific task. They help organize logic and avoid repetition.

slides.title: Defining Methods
slides.content: A method needs an access modifier, return type, name, parameters, and a body in curly braces.

slides.title: Method Return Types
slides.content: A method can return a value using the return keyword. The type must match the declared return type.

exercise.prompt: Use return to send back a value: `return a + b;` - the method must not be _____

slides.title: Void Methods
slides.content: Void methods perform actions but do not return a value. They use return; only to exit early.

slides.title: Calling Methods
slides.content: Call a method by its name followed by parentheses. Pass arguments that match the parameter types.

slides.title: Method Overloading
slides.content: Multiple methods can share the same name if they have different parameter lists. This is called overloading.

exercise.prompt: Same name, different parameters is called _____

slides.title: Parameters and Arguments
slides.content: Parameters are variables in the method definition. Arguments are the actual values passed when calling.

slides.title: Best Practices
slides.content: Use meaningful method names. Keep methods short and focused. Return values instead of printing when possible.

exercise.prompt: Write a method Square that returns the square of an int, then call it with 6
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: return
When run, your code should output: 36

slides.title: Flow Builder: Methods
slides.content: Use the Flow Builder to call a method with arguments.
